name: Cook Islands
summary: The Cook Islands is an asset-protection jurisdiction: its International Trusts Act 1984 and Foundations Act 2012 say foreign forced-heirship rights do not invalidate a trust or a foundation. Ordinary local succession law was not confirmed in this research. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
family_claims: No family-provision statute was confirmed; the Cook Islands applies NZ-derived law in part and the position was not verified.
foreign_law_note: Conflict rules for succession were not sourced. Separately, the International Trusts Act 1984 and Foundations Act 2012 provide that foreign heirship law cannot be used to void a trust or foundation or the transfers into it.
trust_note: International Trusts Act 1984 (asset-protection trust law, heirship claims cannot void a trust) and Foundations Act 2012 (foundation as body corporate). Foreign trusts are recognised on general common-law principles; tax treatment of foreign trusts was not sourced. Trust-industry factsheets are promotional.
open_questions: Local intestacy and wills law (Cook Islands Act 1915 and successors) and any family provision or Family Protection Act equivalent were not sourced.
Domestic tax treatment of foreign trusts and foundations.
The HCCH table as retrieved shows no entry for this jurisdiction (the retrieved copy was marked last updated 2017 and its territorial-extension notes could not be read); re-check the live table.
